# Sentia: Web Render Finish

Status: active for wo-gh-14
Slug: web-render-finish

## Roles
- implementer: builds the change described here
- reviewer: checks the change against this spec
- qa: checks the scenarios below with tests
- product_owner: owns the purpose and accepts the result

## Purpose

The take apart page's product is right and its page is wrong. wo-gh-12 replaced the block primitives with a Blender built Patch One whose identity passes the same product test and whose Blender beauty renders meet the boards' bar. But the owner judged the finish in the page's own web rendering, and two problems survive there, both named by reviewer-design in wo-gh-12's loopback round:

1. Board finishes. In the bundled browser rendering, the sensing and processing board's shield, battery and sensor faces read as flat gray surfaces with little metallic highlight variation, even though the board's geometry is now dense and manufactured (217 meshes, nine finishes in the asset).
2. Cover finish. The silicone micrograin the build generates and the recessed LED socket with its teal emitter exist in the asset and read in the Blender beauty renders, but wash out in the page beats: the cover reads uniformly smooth and the LED slot reads gray, with no readable teal emitter or optical highlight, under the page's unchanged flat lighting.

Production still serves the older procedural build (version 4515d731, from the wo-gh-11 bundling fix), so none of the modeled product is live yet. This order closes the two finish problems where they are judged, in the bundled browser rendering, and then deploys. The builder may work both sides of the problem: asset materials inside the deterministic Blender build, and the take apart client's lighting and material handling. This spec supersedes two clauses of .openspec/specs/take-apart-product-model/spec.md for this order only: its statement that the page's studio lighting does not change, and its no deployment stance (deployment here is the operator's gated step after an approved verdict, per the owner's order for this work order; it is still not part of the line). The governing specs otherwise stay .openspec/specs/take-apart/spec.md, .openspec/specs/take-apart-bundling/spec.md and .openspec/specs/take-apart-product-model/spec.md. The builder and reviewer-design run on GPT-6 Astra; the spec writer, test writer and the other reviewers run on claude-sonnet-5-5, per ANVIL policy.

## References

- design/reference/product-reference.png: the identity anchor (matte off white square patch, strongly rounded corners, SENTIA wordmark, teal LED line).
- design/reference/quality-board-1.png and design/reference/quality-board-2.png: the quality anchor for materials (matte silicone, porous foam, a detailed PCB with real component finishes, translucent films).
- evidence/take-apart-product-model/render-assembled.png and render-exploded.png: the wo-gh-12 beauty renders that pass the boards' bar; what the page rendering must now match in the two named areas.
- runs/wo-gh-12/: the loopback round's reviewer-design output naming the two surviving problems, and the round's evidence (GLB at 798,092 bytes, reproducibility log, bundled browser pass).

## Requirements

### Judged in production shape

- R1 (the page rendering is the evidence): Both problems are judged on the bundled browser rendering of the take apart page (the production shape of wo-gh-11: the production bundle built clean, the bundled output served by a local Worker runtime, beats captured by scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs against that output). The Blender beauty renders are supporting evidence only; a finish that reads in a beauty render but not in the page beats is not closed.

### The two problems

- R2 (board finishes read): In the page rendering, the board's shield, battery and sensor faces no longer read as one flat gray. Metal, solder and package finishes read distinctly under the page's lighting: brightness and reflectance variation across the metal faces, the gold toned pads and terminals visible as metal, the sensor discs reading as metal sensors, package finishes differentiated from the substrate and from each other.
- R3 (cover finish reads): In the page rendering, the cover's silicone micrograin is readable as a fine surface grain that breaks the uniformly smooth read at beat resolution, and the LED reads as a recessed teal emitter inside its socket: the teal is visible in the assembled and mid beats, with the socket's depth shadow around it. The wordmark stays exactly as approved in wo-gh-12.

### Means

- R4 (client lighting and material handling are in scope): The builder may change the take apart client's lighting rig, tone mapping, exposure, environment lighting and on load material adjustments (for example per material metalness, roughness or env map intensity handling) in src/take-apart-client.js. Frozen on the client: what it binds and when (the state function, node binding by name, per frame position and opacity rules, tour, controls, gauges, chart, callouts, quality tiers, fallback), the vendored three.js bytes, and all page chrome and copy in src/take-apart-page.js, which does not change.
- R5 (asset discipline): Any asset change is produced only by blender/build_patch_one.py through the deterministic entry blender/build_all.py (headless Blender pinned 4.5.15, smoke gated by the workflow, rerun after the line before the suite). No hand edited GLB, no downloaded model or texture. If the asset changes, reproducibility is re-proven: two consecutive exports byte identical, and the committed src/patch-one-glb.js bytes equal the export byte for byte. The GLB measures at or under 819,200 bytes on the final tree, with the measured size stated in the test output and the run report. The current asset is 798,092 bytes, so any addition trades bytes through texture or geometry discipline; the budget does not move.
- R6 (the product stays frozen): The five top level nodes keep their exact FACTS names, stack order and translations (layerCenterMm at t=0 within 0.01); layer thicknesses and the 36 mm footprint are unchanged; the wordmark and the LED's position and proportions are unchanged. The identity gate of wo-gh-12 must stay passed: reviewer-design re-runs the same product test and identity must hold on the beauty renders and on the contact sheet.

### Evidence

- R7 (before and after): The builder captures the bundled page beats twice through the capture of record: BEFORE, from the tree at this order's setup commit (unmodified client and asset), and AFTER, from the final tree. Both sets, with their browser pass logs recording zero console and page errors, are committed under evidence/web-render-finish/before/ and evidence/web-render-finish/after/, composed into contact sheets the same way as evidence/take-apart/. The standard capture also regenerates evidence/take-apart/ on the final tree, and the beauty renders under evidence/take-apart-product-model/ are regenerated if the asset changed. The builder's output compares before and after per problem and records what it adjusted.
- R8 (production shape, standing): The production bundle command succeeds on the final tree with zero local patches, command and exit status recorded. The bundled output served locally records zero console errors and zero page errors, the scene ready flag set, the GLB route fetched, the five named nodes present in the loaded scene, and a screenshot whose scene region shows the rendered product. No evidence step (before beats, after beats, standard capture, pass logs) imports or loads the unbundled source; every capture drives the bundled output only.
- R9 (suite): The project suite passes on the final tree, including the take apart tests and the product model tests in their original meaning, and the new tests of this order. The one known exception: the design v4 S11 test failure, pre existing on this branch's base and resolved on the sibling branch anvil/run-s11-rebaseline (wo-gh-10, approved), is itemized by name in the run report, never silently absorbed and never fixed by editing another run's evidence.

const BASE_GLB = { bytes: 798092, sha256: '3a84576570cf0ec95fb85885ecfc7d831927237ef54d167d4d37ad7baea19c58' };
const BASE_MODULE_SHA = 'aea8040575ffa9ce600ed7db779e911d48ee4f49d87192a841e4180ab2ce7132';
const NAMES = FACTS.layers.map((l) => l.name);
const BEATS = ['assembled', 'mid', 'apart', 'board', 'xray'];

const root = (rel) => new URL('../' + rel, import.meta.url);
const exists = (rel) => fs.existsSync(root(rel));
const read = (rel) => fs.readFileSync(root(rel), 'utf8');
const sha = (buf) => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest('hex');
const get = (p) => worker.fetch(new Request('https://sentia.test' + p));

const setupReachable = () => {
  try { execFileSync('git', ['cat-file', '-e', SETUP_COMMIT + '^{commit}'], { stdio: 'ignore' }); return true; } catch { return false; }
};
const git = (...args) => execFileSync('git', args, { encoding: 'utf8' });

function parseGlb(buf) {
  assert.equal(buf.readUInt32LE(0), 0x46546c67, 'GLB magic "glTF"');
  assert.equal(buf.readUInt32LE(8), buf.length, 'GLB header length equals byte length');
  const jlen = buf.readUInt32LE(12);
  assert.equal(buf.readUInt32LE(16), 0x4e4f534a, 'first chunk is JSON');
  return JSON.parse(buf.toString('utf8', 20, 20 + jlen));
}
async function moduleInfo() {
  assert.ok(exists('src/patch-one-glb.js'), 'src/patch-one-glb.js is missing');
  const mod = await import('../src/patch-one-glb.js');
  const b64 = Object.values(mod).find((v) => typeof v === 'string');
  assert.ok(b64, 'src/patch-one-glb.js exports the base64 string');
  const bytes = Buffer.from(b64, 'base64');
  return { bytes, glbSha: sha(bytes), moduleSha: sha(fs.readFileSync(root('src/patch-one-glb.js'))) };
}
const assetChanged = async () => (await moduleInfo()).glbSha !== BASE_GLB.sha256;

// World bounds of a subtree from POSITION accessor min and max (nodes carry translation only here;
// the frozen product test in take-apart-product-model keeps the full matrix reader).
function worldBounds(gltf, idx, off = [0, 0, 0]) {
  const n = gltf.nodes[idx];
  const t = n.translation || [0, 0, 0];
  const o = [off[0] + t[0], off[1] + t[1], off[2] + t[2]];
  const lo = [Infinity, Infinity, Infinity], hi = [-Infinity, -Infinity, -Infinity];
  const add = (l, h) => { for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { lo[i] = Math.min(lo[i], l[i]); hi[i] = Math.max(hi[i], h[i]); } };
  if (n.mesh != null) {
    assert.ok(!n.rotation && !n.scale && !n.matrix, 'descendant nodes are plain translations');
    for (const p of gltf.meshes[n.mesh].primitives) {
      const a = gltf.accessors[p.attributes.POSITION];
      add(a.min.map((v, i) => v + o[i]), a.max.map((v, i) => v + o[i]));
    }
  }
  for (const c of n.children || []) { const b = worldBounds(gltf, c, o); if (b) add(b.lo, b.hi); }
  return lo[0] === Infinity ? null : { lo, hi };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S1 (R5)
test('web-render-finish S1: the GLB served at /models/patch-one.glb is at or under 819,200 bytes, size stated', async () => {
  const res = await get('/models/patch-one.glb');
  assert.equal(res.status, 200);
  const served = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());
  console.log(`# patch-one.glb measured size (web-render-finish): ${served.length} bytes (${(served.length / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB), budget ${BUDGET} bytes`);
  assert.ok(served.length <= BUDGET, `GLB is ${served.length} bytes, over the ${BUDGET} byte budget`);
  assert.ok(served.equals((await moduleInfo()).bytes), 'served bytes equal the decoded asset module');
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S2 (R6)
test('web-render-finish S2: five FACTS nodes in stack order at layerCenterMm(t=0) within 0.01, 36 mm footprint, 2.5 mm profile', async () => {
  const { bytes } = await moduleInfo();
  const gltf = parseGlb(bytes);
  const top = gltf.scenes[gltf.scene ?? 0].nodes;
  assert.deepEqual(top.map((i) => gltf.nodes[i].name), NAMES, 'exactly the five FACTS names in stack order');
  top.forEach((idx, k) => {
    const t = gltf.nodes[idx].translation || [0, 0, 0];
    assert.ok(Math.abs(t[0]) <= 0.01 && Math.abs(t[2]) <= 0.01, `${NAMES[k]} x and z are 0`);
    assert.ok(Math.abs(t[1] - M.layerCenterMm(k, 0)) <= 0.01, `${NAMES[k]} y ${t[1]} vs layerCenterMm ${M.layerCenterMm(k, 0)}`);
  });
  const lo = [Infinity, Infinity, Infinity], hi = [-Infinity, -Infinity, -Infinity];
  for (const idx of top) {
    const b = worldBounds(gltf, idx);
    for (let a = 0; a < 3; a++) { lo[a] = Math.min(lo[a], b.lo[a]); hi[a] = Math.max(hi[a], b.hi[a]); }
  }
  assert.ok(Math.abs(hi[0] - lo[0] - 36) <= 0.5, `footprint x ${(hi[0] - lo[0]).toFixed(3)}`);
  assert.ok(Math.abs(hi[2] - lo[2] - 36) <= 0.5, `footprint z ${(hi[2] - lo[2]).toFixed(3)}`);
  assert.ok(Math.abs(hi[1] - lo[1] - 2.5) <= 0.1, `profile ${(hi[1] - lo[1]).toFixed(3)}`);
  // Layer thicknesses are frozen (local bounds of each layer, descendants only).
  top.forEach((idx, k) => {
    const n = gltf.nodes[idx];
    const kids = (n.children || []).map((c) => worldBounds(gltf, c));
    const l = Math.min(...kids.map((b) => b.lo[1])), h = Math.max(...kids.map((b) => b.hi[1]));
    const slack = k === 4 ? 0.3 : 0.1;
    assert.ok(h - l >= M.LAYERS[k].thicknessMm * 0.4 && h - l <= M.LAYERS[k].thicknessMm + slack, `${NAMES[k]} thickness ${(h - l).toFixed(3)}`);
  });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S3 (R5)
test('web-render-finish S3: asset unchanged equals the wo-gh-12 loopback asset; asset changed has reproducibility re-proven', async () => {
  const info = await moduleInfo();
  if (!(await assetChanged())) {
    assert.equal(info.bytes.length, BASE_GLB.bytes, 'unchanged asset keeps its byte size');
    assert.equal(info.moduleSha, BASE_MODULE_SHA, 'committed module is byte identical to the wo-gh-12 loopback asset');
    return;
  }
  const log = 'evidence/web-render-finish/reproducibility.log';
  assert.ok(exists(log), `${log} is missing: the asset changed, reproducibility must be re-proven`);
  const text = read(log);
  const exports = [...text.matchAll(/export\s+(\d+)[^\n]*GLB SHA256 ([0-9a-f]{64})[^\n]*bytes (\d+)[^\n]*exit 0/gi)];
  assert.ok(exports.length >= 2, 'the log records two consecutive full build_all.py exports, each exit 0');
  assert.equal(exports[0][2], exports[1][2], 'two exports have the same GLB SHA256');
  assert.equal(exports[0][2], info.glbSha, 'the export SHA256 equals the committed GLB bytes');
  assert.equal(Number(exports[0][3]), info.bytes.length, 'the logged byte size equals the committed GLB size');
  const mods = [...text.matchAll(/module SHA256 ([0-9a-f]{64})/gi)].map((m) => m[1]);
  assert.ok(mods.length >= 2 && mods.every((m) => m === info.moduleSha), 'committed src/patch-one-glb.js equals the export module byte for byte');
  assert.match(text, /PASS/);
  assert.match(text, /4\.5\.15/, 'the log names the pinned Blender 4.5.15');
});

test('web-render-finish R5: asset changes come only from the deterministic Blender build, no downloaded model or texture', () => {
  const py = read('blender/build_patch_one.py') + read('blender/build_all.py');

  if (changed) assert.match(git('diff', '--name-only', SETUP_COMMIT, '--', 'blender/build_patch_one.py').trim(), /build_patch_one\.py/, 'a changed GLB module comes with a changed build script (no hand edit)');
});

test('web-render-finish R2-R4: the run changed the finish somewhere it may: the client rendering or the asset build', async () => {
  if (!setupReachable()) return;
  const diff = git('diff', '--name-only', SETUP_COMMIT, '--', 'src/take-apart-client.js', 'blender/build_patch_one.py', 'src/patch-one-glb.js').trim();
  assert.ok(diff, 'neither src/take-apart-client.js nor the asset build changed: the finish problems cannot be closed');
  // The client work is real, not a comment edit: the diff must touch rendering code lines.
  const cd = git('diff', '-U0', SETUP_COMMIT, '--', 'src/take-apart-client.js');
  if (cd) {
    const code = cd.split('\n').filter((l) => /^[+-](?![+-])/.test(l) && !/^[+-]\s*(\/\/|\/\*|\*)/.test(l) && l.trim().length > 1);
    assert.ok(code.length > 0, 'client diff has code lines');
  }
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S4, S5, S6 evidence (R7), judged by reviewer-design
const isPng = (b) => b.length > 8 && b.readUInt32BE(0) === 0x89504e47 && b.readUInt32BE(4) === 0x0d0a1a0a;
const pngSize = (b) => ({ w: b.readUInt32BE(16), h: b.readUInt32BE(20) });

test('web-render-finish R7: before and after beats and contact sheets are committed, valid PNGs of the same size', () => {
  for (const set of ['before', 'after']) {
    for (const f of [...BEATS.map((b) => `beat-${b}.png`), 'contact-sheet.png']) {
      const rel = `evidence/web-render-finish/${set}/${f}`;
      assert.ok(exists(rel), `${rel} is missing`);
      const b = fs.readFileSync(root(rel));
      assert.ok(isPng(b), `${rel} is a PNG`);
      assert.ok(pngSize(b).w >= 800 && pngSize(b).h >= 400, `${rel} is at least beat resolution, got ${pngSize(b).w}x${pngSize(b).h}`);
    }
  }
  for (const b of [...BEATS.map((x) => `beat-${x}.png`), 'contact-sheet.png']) {
    const be = fs.readFileSync(root(`evidence/web-render-finish/before/${b}`)), af = fs.readFileSync(root(`evidence/web-render-finish/after/${b}`));
    assert.deepEqual(pngSize(be), pngSize(af), `${b} before and after share dimensions (same capture of record)`);
  }
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S7 (R8)
function passLogChecks(rel, label) {
  assert.ok(exists(rel), `${rel} is missing`);
  const log = read(rel);
  assert.match(log, /console errors: 0\b/, `${label}: zero console errors`);
  assert.match(log, /page errors: 0\b/, `${label}: zero page errors`);
  assert.match(log, /scene ready: true/, `${label}: scene ready`);
  assert.match(log, /GLB \/models\/patch-one\.glb: status 200; bytes (\d+)/, `${label}: GLB route fetched`);
  const bytes = Number(log.match(/GLB \/models\/patch-one\.glb: status 200; bytes (\d+)/)[1]);
  assert.ok(bytes <= BUDGET, `${label}: logged GLB bytes ${bytes} within budget`);
  const nodes = log.match(/loaded nodes: 5; ([^\n]+)/);
  assert.ok(nodes, `${label}: five loaded nodes recorded`);
  assert.deepEqual(nodes[1].split(';').map((s) => s.trim()), NAMES, `${label}: the five named nodes are recorded`);
  assert.match(log, /Bundled Worker:/, `${label}: the capture drove the bundled Worker output`);
  assert.doesNotMatch(log, /src\/take-apart-client\.js|src\/index\.js/, `${label}: no unbundled source loaded`);
  return log;
}

test('web-render-finish S7: before and after browser pass logs record zero errors, scene ready, GLB fetched, five named nodes, bundled output', () => {
  passLogChecks('evidence/web-render-finish/before/browser-pass.log', 'before');
  const after = passLogChecks('evidence/web-render-finish/after/browser-pass.log', 'after');
  assert.match(after, /gauge comparison: PASS/, 'after: gauge comparison passes');
  passLogChecks('evidence/take-apart/browser-pass.log', 'standard capture');
});

  for (const [re, what] of [
    [/TakeApartModel/, 'state function binding'],

    [/tour/i, 'tour'],
    [/OrbitControls|controls|pointer/i, 'controls'],
    [/quality|tier|pixelRatio|setPixelRatio/i, 'quality tiers'],
    [/fallback|catch/i, 'fallback'],
    [/sceneReady/, 'scene ready flag'],
  ]) assert.match(src, re, `${what} survives in the client`);
  if (!setupReachable()) return;
  // Removed lines may only be rendering ones: the frozen binding identifiers must not disappear.
  const removed = git('diff', '-U0', SETUP_COMMIT, '--', 'src/take-apart-client.js').split('\n').filter((l) => /^-(?!--)/.test(l)).join('\n');
  for (const id of ['sceneReady', 'TakeApartModel', 'getObjectByName', 'gaugeReadout', 'layerCenterMm', 'tour']) {
    if (removed.includes(id)) assert.ok(src.includes(id), `frozen identifier ${id} was removed from the client`);

test('web-render-finish S10: the run diff against the setup commit names only the allowed paths', () => {
  if (!setupReachable()) return; // not reachable in this checkout; the run gate checks scope
  const tracked = git('diff', '--name-only', SETUP_COMMIT);
  const untracked = git('ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard');
  const names = (tracked + untracked).split('\n').filter(Boolean).filter((n) => !HARNESS_FILES.has(n))
    .filter((n) => n !== '.openspec/specs/web-render-finish/spec.md'); // operator setup, not part of the line
  const allowed = [
    /^blender\/build_patch_one\.py$/,
    /^src\/patch-one-glb\.js$/,
    /^src\/take-apart-client\.js$/,
    /^tests\/web-render-finish\.test\.js$/,
    /^tests\/take-apart-product-model\.test\.js$/,
    /^tests\/take-apart\.test\.js$/,
    /^scripts\/capture-take-apart\.mjs$/,
    /^evidence\/web-render-finish\//,
    /^evidence\/take-apart\//,
    /^evidence\/take-apart-product-model\//,
    /^runs\/wo-gh-14\//,
  ];
  const outside = names.filter((n) => !allowed.some((re) => re.test(n)));
  assert.deepEqual(outside, [], 'files outside the allowed scope');
});

def silicone_texture(mat):
    # Generated silicone grain: seeded normal tile, no silhouette displacement.
    rng=random.Random(4515);size=128
    heights=[rng.uniform(-1,1) for _ in range(size*size)]
    pixels=[]
    for y in range(size):
        for x in range(size):
            dx=heights[y*size+(x+1)%size]-heights[y*size+(x-1)%size]
            dy=heights[((y+1)%size)*size+x]-heights[((y-1)%size)*size+x]
            v=Vector((dx*.24,dy*.24,1)).normalized()
            pixels.extend((v.x*.5+.5,v.y*.5+.5,v.z*.5+.5,1))
    img=bpy.data.images.new('Generated silicone micrograin normals',width=size,height=size)
    img.colorspace_settings.name='Non-Color';img.pixels=pixels;img.pack()
    nt=mat.node_tree;tex=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexImage');tex.image=img
    uv=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord');mapping=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeMapping')
    mapping.inputs['Scale'].default_value=(8,8,1)
    nt.links.new(uv.outputs['UV'],mapping.inputs['Vector']);nt.links.new(mapping.outputs[0],tex.inputs['Vector'])
    normal=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeNormalMap');normal.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.65
    nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Color'],normal.inputs['Color']);nt.links.new(normal.outputs[0],nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF').inputs['Normal'])


def copper_run(parent,mat,points,width=.085):
    for a,b in zip(points,points[1:]):
        dx,dy=b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]
        o=box('Routed copper trace',parent,mat,((a[0]+b[0])/2,(a[1]+b[1])/2,-.043),(math.hypot(dx,dy)+width,width,.012),0)
        o.rotation_euler.z=math.atan2(dy,dx)

    box('Recessed optical lens',parents[0],glass,(0,-3.2,.242),(9.8,.67,.028),.012)
    shell('Microcell comfort foam',parents[1],foam,[(.985,-.35),(1,-.28),(1,.27),(.985,.35)])
    shell('PCB substrate',parents[2],pcb,[(.965,-.25),(.965,-.06)])

    box('Thin film battery',b,metal,(7,4,.075),(9,12,.3),.06)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- PNG pixels
function decodePng(buf) {
  assert.ok(buf.subarray(0, 8).equals(Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a])), 'not a PNG');
  let off = 8, w, h, bpp, idat = [];
  while (off < buf.length) {
    const len = buf.readUInt32BE(off), type = buf.toString('ascii', off + 4, off + 8);
    const data = buf.subarray(off + 8, off + 8 + len);
    if (type === 'IHDR') {
      w = data.readUInt32BE(0); h = data.readUInt32BE(4);
      assert.equal(data[8], 8, '8 bit PNG expected'); assert.equal(data[12], 0, 'non interlaced PNG expected');
      bpp = { 2: 3, 6: 4 }[data[9]]; assert.ok(bpp, 'RGB or RGBA PNG expected');
    } else if (type === 'IDAT') idat.push(data);
    else if (type === 'IEND') break;
    off += 12 + len;
  }
  const raw = zlib.inflateSync(Buffer.concat(idat)), stride = w * bpp, px = Buffer.alloc(h * stride);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    const f = raw[y * (stride + 1)], row = raw.subarray(y * (stride + 1) + 1, (y + 1) * (stride + 1));
    for (let x = 0; x < stride; x++) {
      const a = x >= bpp ? px[y * stride + x - bpp] : 0, b = y ? px[(y - 1) * stride + x] : 0, c = x >= bpp && y ? px[(y - 1) * stride + x - bpp] : 0;
      const p = a + b - c, pa = Math.abs(p - a), pb = Math.abs(p - b), pc = Math.abs(p - c);
      const pred = [0, a, b, (a + b) >> 1, pa <= pb && pa <= pc ? a : pb <= pc ? b : c][f];
      px[y * stride + x] = (row[x] + pred) & 255;
    }
  }
  return { w, h, bpp, px };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- S6 structure (R11)
for (const name of ['render-assembled.png', 'render-exploded.png']) {
  test(`product-model R11/S6: ${name} exists, is at least 800 by 800, sits on the brand paper #FAFAF6 and shows a rendered product`, () => {
    assert.ok(fs.existsSync(new URL(name, EVID)), `evidence/take-apart-product-model/${name} is missing`);
    const bytes = fs.readFileSync(new URL(name, EVID));
    assert.ok(bytes.length >= 30 * 1024, `${name} is ${bytes.length} bytes`);
    const { w, h, bpp, px } = decodePng(bytes);
    assert.ok(w >= 800 && h >= 800, `${name} is ${w}x${h}`);
    const at = (x, y) => [0, 1, 2].map((c) => px[(y * w + x) * bpp + c]);
    for (const [x, y] of [[2, 2], [w - 3, 2], [2, h - 3], [w - 3, h - 3]]) {
      at(x, y).forEach((v, c) => assert.ok(Math.abs(v - [0xfa, 0xfa, 0xf6][c]) <= 4, `${name} corner (${x},${y}) channel ${c} is ${v}, brand paper is ${[0xfa, 0xfa, 0xf6][c]}`));
test('take-apart scope: the run touches no file outside the allowed list', () => {
  let names;
  try {
    execFileSync('git', ['cat-file', '-e', SETUP_COMMIT + '^{commit}'], { stdio: 'ignore' });
    const tracked = execFileSync('git', ['diff', '--name-only', SETUP_COMMIT], { encoding: 'utf8' });
    const untracked = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
    names = (tracked + untracked).split('\n').filter(Boolean).filter((n) => !HARNESS_FILES.has(n));
  } catch {
    return;
  }
  const allowed = [
    /^src\/take-apart-(model|model-browser|page|client)\.js$/,
    /^src\/vendor-three\.js$/,
    /^src\/index\.js$/,
    /^src\/page\.js$/,
    /^tests\/take-apart\.test\.js$/,
    /^scripts\/capture-take-apart\.mjs$/,
    /^evidence\/take-apart\//,
    /^runs\/wo-gh-9\//,
  ];
  const outside = names.filter((n) => !allowed.some((re) => re.test(n)));
  assert.deepEqual(outside, [], 'files outside the allowed scope');
});

def material(name, rgb, roughness=.7, metallic=0, alpha=1):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes = True
    p = m.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    p.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (*rgb, alpha)
    p.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = roughness
    p.inputs['Metallic'].default_value = metallic
    if alpha < 1:
        p.inputs['Alpha'].default_value = alpha
        m.surface_render_method = 'DITHERED'
    return m


def attach(obj, name, parent, mat):
    obj.name = name
    obj.parent = parent
    obj.data.materials.append(mat)
    return obj

 succeeded in 0ms:
def attach(obj, name, parent, mat):
    obj.name = name
    obj.parent = parent
    obj.data.materials.append(mat)
    return obj


def outline(a=18, r=9, count=16):
    points = []
    for cx, cy, start in [(a-r,a-r,0),(-a+r,a-r,90),(-a+r,-a+r,180),(a-r,-a+r,270)]:
        for i in range(count):
            angle = math.radians(start+i*90/(count-1))
            points.append((cx+r*math.cos(angle),cy+r*math.sin(angle)))
    return points


def shell(name, parent, mat, rings, peel=False):
    pts = outline()
    verts = []
    for scale, z in rings:
        for x,y in pts:
            lift = .12 * max(0, (x-y-21)/9)**2 if peel else 0
            verts.append((x*scale,y*scale,z+lift))
    n = len(pts)
    faces = [tuple(reversed(range(n)))]
    for j in range(len(rings)-1):
        for i in range(n):
            k=(i+1)%n
            faces.append((j*n+i,j*n+k,(j+1)*n+k,(j+1)*n+i))
    faces.append(tuple(range((len(rings)-1)*n,len(rings)*n)))
    mesh=bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    mesh.from_pydata(verts,[],faces); mesh.update()
    obj=bpy.data.objects.new(name,mesh); bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
    attach(obj,name,parent,mat)
    for p in mesh.polygons: p.use_smooth = len(p.vertices)==4
    uv=mesh.uv_layers.new(name='UVMap')
    for poly in mesh.polygons:
        for index in poly.loop_indices:
            co=mesh.vertices[mesh.loops[index].vertex_index].co
            if len(poly.vertices)==4:
                uv.data[index].uv=((co.x+co.y+36)/36,co.z/9)
            else:
                uv.data[index].uv=((co.x+18)/36,(co.y+18)/36)
    return obj


def box(name,parent,mat,xyz,size,bevel=.025):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1,location=xyz)
    o=bpy.context.object; o.dimensions=size
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False,rotation=False,scale=True)
    if bevel:
        mod=o.modifiers.new('Machined edges','BEVEL');mod.width=bevel;mod.segments=1
        bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
        mod=o.modifiers.new('Weighted normals','WEIGHTED_NORMAL')
        bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
    # Bevel interpolates unused cube UVs with tiny run-dependent rounding.
    # These untextured parts need no UVs; remove them for byte-identical exports.
    for uv in list(o.data.uv_layers):o.data.uv_layers.remove(uv)
    return attach(o,name,parent,mat)

# Web render finish — builder evidence

The implementation changes only material settings and client rendering (S4/S5), with the capture output selection and scope baselines required by S7/S10. Approval and the product identity judgement belong to reviewer-design; this report does not approve the work. No deployment was performed.

Before: the bundled setup client used ambient intensity 1.3, one overhead key and no reflection environment. The cover was smooth at beat resolution and the recessed LED appeared gray. Board metal faces were uniformly gray with weak differentiation from packages.

After: a generated PMREM studio environment supplies three luminous reflection cards against a dark surround. Ambient fill is .25, the key is lower and a cool rim separates edges; exposure is .95. Metals receive stronger environment reflections than dielectric materials. The shield and battery now have bright bevels and darker reflective faces; solder highlights, gold pads and sensor edges separate from the dark substrate and epoxy packages. The Blender plated-contact material has warmer gold color and lower roughness. The lighting is generated locally without external images or changes to vendored three.js.

Cover: the same seeded normal tile repeats twice instead of eight times, preventing its grain being averaged away at beat resolution, and exported normal strength is .85. Client shading attenuates side grain to compensate for the study's frozen ×8 vertical exaggeration while retaining fine crown grain. The emitter's exported strength increases from .5 to 1.4. The optical lens carries teal emission and has increased optical opacity, so the emitter's color survives the deep, vertically exaggerated pocket in the hero view. Its geometry, position and proportions are unchanged; the socket border remains recessed. The wordmark is untouched.

The GLB is 798,088 bytes (budget 819,200), four bytes smaller than the baseline. Two consecutive full Blender 4.5.15 builds exited 0 and generated byte-identical modules. See reproducibility.log and the full build logs. frozen-product.log compares nodes, meshes, accessors, scenes and the entire binary payload against setup: all identical. Only GLB material JSON differs. Both beauty renders were regenerated.

Before evidence is captured from an archive of operator setup 62f98b32144b2e64fd0227d4ff403d67e777bec3, with its original client and original 798,092-byte asset. The only capture-script changes select an output directory and also record the standard browser log. The first baseline browser process closed before completing the tour; the complete rerun replaces that partial evidence. Intermediate finish captures are replaced by the final capture. All captures build with Wrangler deploy --dry-run and serve that built Worker with --no-bundle; none imports the unbundled page or client.

The test setup constants now point to this round's actual operator setup, 62f98b3. The previous 4de668a and 7748273 objects are unavailable in this checkout, which otherwise silently skips scope assertions.
